hook.title: 455 TONS
hook.sub: stood up with sand. one chance.

beats.vo: Four hundred fifty-five tons of granite, stood up with sand.
No crane. No engine. One chance to get it right.
Drag it up a ramp, to a pit full of sand.
As the pit empties, the obelisk tilts under its own weight.
The last degrees: ropes, hundreds of men, and no second chance.
The biggest one ever attempted cracked in the quarry.
One thousand ninety tons. Still lying there, three thousand years later.
Should we finish it today? A or B.

cta.title: FINISH IT TODAY?
cta.b: No — leave it in the rock

metadata.title: Egypt Stood Up a 455-TON Obelisk With SAND 🏛️ Should we finish the broken one?
metadata.description:
No crane, no engine: drag the obelisk to a sand-filled pit, let the sand out slowly, and gravity tilts 455 tons of granite onto its pedestal — with one chance to get it right. The biggest one ever attempted (1,090 t) cracked and still lies in the Aswan quarry.

3D reconstruction by Ancient Tech. Should we finish it today? Comment A or B.

Sources: Engelbach, 'The Problem of the Obelisks' (1923); NOVA 'Secrets of Lost Empires'.
metadata.pinned_comment:
The 1,090-ton Unfinished Obelisk still lies cracked in Aswan. Finish it with modern cranes? A = yes, B = leave it 👇
